archival_memory.archie_age: Archie is three years old now.
archival_memory.archie_puppy: I vividly remember how he'd tumble over himself trying to figure out 'sit' and 'stay.' It's wild how big he's gotten now.
archival_memory.video_calls: I video call my parents almost daily, and Archie always seems to recognize my voice.
archival_memory.family_influence: My dad is a software engineer, and he's part of the reason I got into computer science in the first place. We used to do these small coding exercises together when I was in high school. He'd challenge me to figure out a puzzle or a problem, and it sparked that early fascination with logic and technology that eventually led me to major in CS. My mom, on the other hand, works as a nurse. She's the most caring person I know, and she's always the emotional backbone of our family. Even if it's late at night, she'll pick up my calls when I need a pep talk or if I'm worried about an upcoming exam. Between my parents, I found this healthy balance: I got the analytical edge from my dad and the empathetic side from my mom. My sister, well, she's just a ball of energy—constantly on social media, playing new games, or looking for the next big trend. She's so plugged into technology that sometimes she jokes she's going to overshadow me in the tech scene. She might be right.
archival_memory.family_traditions: One of our family traditions is going on a Saturday morning hike whenever I'm in town. We pack some snacks, load Archie into our SUV, and drive out to this trail about twenty minutes away. The path isn't super long, but it has a great view at the summit of a small bluff that overlooks a lake. Archie loves it—he's got endless energy. By the time we're at the top, he's chasing squirrels and sniffing every tree. Watching him run around like that reminds me to appreciate the small things. I can get so wrapped up in code and classes that I forget to just breathe and enjoy nature.
archival_memory.grandma_teasing: My grandma still teases me about the time I broke her antique vase when I was in middle school by throwing a mini football around her living room. I try to tune out that story, even though it's retold almost every Thanksgiving.
archival_memory.family_holidays: Holiday gatherings are a big deal in my family. Thanksgiving is practically a potluck extravaganza, with all kinds of dishes that make you want to hibernate until Christmas. Archie, of course, tries to snag anything that drops on the floor. We learned the hard way he has a sensitive stomach—one year he got into some leftover turkey bones, and we had to make a late-night veterinary visit. Ever since then, we're super careful about what 'people food' he can get his paws on.
archival_memory.family_influence_on_career: I find it interesting how family shapes who you become. Even though I'm on my own at college, I realize that a lot of the patience and resilience I rely on while working through tough programming projects actually comes from my parents. My dad taught me how to stay calm and break down problems, while my mom showed me how to be patient and empathetic—even when the situation is frustrating, like when a project partner doesn't pull their weight or code isn't cooperating. Plus, I can't forget my sister, who always pushes me to stay up on new trends so I don't become a relic in my twenties. Sometimes I do write about personal stories, like Archie or silly moments with my sister, in my personal statements for scholarships or grad school applications, because they matter to me that much.
archival_memory.family_description: We're supportive, close-knit, and lively. The way they come together around Archie, fussing over him or laughing at his antics, shows me what unconditional love looks like. I may be a busy fourth-year with internship interviews, clubs, research, and everything else on my plate, but at the end of the day, it's nice to know there's a place—and a family—where I'm always welcome, dog hair and all. I think that's what keeps me going, to be honest. No matter how many lines of code fail to compile, I can always count on home to recharge me. And yes, that definitely includes Archie leaping into my arms the second I walk through the door.
